newsDocuments.headline: Oil prices steady as Middle East shipping attacks counter supply surplus outlook

segments.text: BEIJING/SINGAPORE: Oil prices steadied on Thursday after losses in the prior session as expectations for a market surplus outweighed lingering worries about Middle East supply amid attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz .
Brent crude futures were trading up 5 cents, or 0.05%, at $92 a barrel as of 0455 GMT.

Brent fell 1.3% in the previous session while WTI dropped 3.2% to its lowest since August 26 on emerging expectations of a supply surplus as crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels.
